prompt: Write a short blog post about why everyone should grow something. Aim for about 400 words. Reply with the post only.
final_message:
# Grow Something, Anything

You don't need a farm. You don't need a green thumb. You don't even need a garden. But I'd argue everyone should grow something, even if it's a single basil plant on a windowsill.

**It resets your sense of time.** Most of our lives run on notifications, deadlines, and same-day delivery. A seed doesn't care. It sprouts when it's ready, and no amount of refreshing speeds it up. Spending a few weeks waiting on a tomato is a gentle, necessary lesson in patience, and it's one we rarely get anywhere else.

**It makes you pay attention.** Growing things means noticing things: the way leaves droop before you've remembered to water, the new shoot that appeared overnight, the slight yellowing that says something's off. That daily habit of looking closely carries over. You start noticing the weather, the seasons, the birds that visit your pots. The world gets a little more vivid.

**It changes how you eat.** A tomato you grew yourself tastes better than any in the store. Part of that is freshness, and part of it is knowing the weeks of effort behind it. You also waste less, because you understand what it took to produce. Kids who grow carrots will often eat carrots, which is a small miracle every parent will appreciate.

**It teaches you to fail gently.** You will kill a plant. Probably several. Aphids will arrive, a frost will surprise you, or you'll go on vacation and come home to a crispy fern. Gardening is low-stakes practice at trying, losing, adjusting, and trying again. Nobody's career was ruined by a dead zucchini, but plenty of people have learned resilience from one.

**It connects you to something bigger.** Every plant is a small ecosystem. Soil microbes, pollinators, worms, and sunlight all take part in what ends up on your plate. Tending even a tiny piece of that makes you a participant in the natural world rather than just a spectator.

**It's good for you.** Studies keep finding that time with plants lowers stress, lifts mood, and gets you outside and moving. Even handling soil seems to have a calming effect. It's one of the cheapest therapies available.

## How to start

Keep it small. Pick one easy plant: herbs like basil, mint, or chives, or leaf lettuce, radishes, or cherry tomatoes. Find a sunny spot, use a decent pot with drainage, and water when the top inch of soil feels dry. That's nearly all there is to it.

Then watch what happens. Within a few weeks, you'll likely find yourself checking on it first thing in the morning, and maybe quietly planning your next one.

Go grow something.
